text:
It was 3:17am at the bakery, all yeast and quiet. Marisol put her first loaves in the oven and spotted the worn copy of The Borrowers in the wicker basket by the back door again. For six weeks every Thursday, someone's been leaving it there instead of the library two blocks over. No name on it, no card. Just the book, smells faintly like rain and woodsmoke.
Tonight she found a note folded between pages 84 and 85. She wiped her floury hands and opened it. I can't make it to the library before closing, please keep it another week, it says. I like knowing it's warm. She stared at the basket, then the tray of cinnamon rolls on the cooling rack. Picked the one with the most icing. Wrapped it in wax paper, tucked the note back into the book, put both by the door. Flipped the sign to open and started the coffee.
